info.title: Aplos Mail engine contract
info.description: Contract v1. Additive changes only within v1. Calls are `POST /v1/call/<Type>/<verb>` with the arguments as the body; a command's `opId` is also the `Idempotency-Key`. A failed call answers with `{error}` and a non-2xx status. Frames stream from `GET /v1/events` (SSE, `id: <seq>`, `Last-Event-ID` resumes). Blobs are `PUT /v1/blob` and `GET /v1/blob/{id}`. Methods marked `x-aplos-ui-only` are refused by the listener.

post.summary: Handshake facts: versions, dbEpoch and state, engine state, capabilities, whether any account exists, the engine clock.
What changed since a state, for catch-up after a reconnect; `cannotCalculateChanges` below the change-log floor or across dbEpochs.
The settings singleton.

Change settings by section; `stateMismatch` when `ifInState` is behind. The `ai` section (providers, their addresses, the paid mark, features, background) and three `mail` fields that change what the owner is exposed to or can undo (`remoteImages`, `imageAllowList`, `undoSendSeconds`) are for Electron windows only.
Open a live window of at most 200 ids over a view; later changes arrive as `window` frames. `holdIds` stay in place.
Scroll a window to a position or anchor, or, for events windows, to another range.
Close a window.
Keep these rows in place (the row under the cursor and its neighbours) until released or about 2 s after the last activity; calling it again is the activity ping.
Release held rows (all when `ids` is absent); the window then reconciles.
A one-shot read of a view (CLI, MCP, Today, Home's "Next:"); no window stays open.
Labels and folders with unread thread counts.
Sidebar counts for every account and each one.
Rows of a `lowSenders` window.
Search the provider once, on Return only; results join the matching search window, progress arrives as `progress` frames.
Body-free thread rows.
Triage: Done, Later, trash, read state, bookmark, due date, reminder, lane and the rest, on ids or a whole view or section, applied in one commit and queued for the provider.
"Why it's here": one sentence and a quote from the mail saying why the thread is in its lane, and who placed it.
The reader opened a thread: fetch it whole if the row is partial (interactive lane) and mark it opened for retention.

Undo an operation: cancel it while held (`undoUntil`), else queue its inverse under `undoOpId`; never a delayed commit. A send is cancelled while queued or scheduled. Needs the scope of the method that made the operation.
The state of operations after their receipts (queued, synced, failed, conflict).
Retry a failed operation (the inline Retry after a rejected write). Needs the scope of the method that made the operation.
Message headers and attachment lists, no bodies.
The plain-text rendering and quote ranges of a body, fetching it if absent. HTML is shown only through `Mail/frame`.
Prefetch bodies on intent (focus or hover) by message, or by thread (the bodies the reader opens with, ARCH AM-1), or cancel a prefetch.

Render a message into the sealed `aplos-mail://` frame: sanitized on read, trackers removed, remote images blocked unless loaded or allowed. Electron windows only: a frame URL means nothing elsewhere, and the 64-token cap is per window.
"Load images from this sender": add an address or `@domain` to `Settings.mail.imageAllowList`, or remove it.
Free a frame token when the reader replaces it.
Re-render a frame with quoted history opened or closed (the O key); returns the new frame.
Make an attachment's bytes available as a blob, fetching it if absent.
The raw message for "Show original" and `.eml` export, fetched live, as a blob.
Upload bytes (an attachment, a dictation) as a transferable `Uint8Array`, never base64; 25 MB at most.
Read a blob's bytes (over HTTP this is `GET /v1/blob/:id`).
Drop a blob the caller no longer needs. A blob attached to a draft with a live send stays until the send settles (FR-7): `stateMismatch` "This file is attached to a message waiting to send."
Drafts, local and from other devices.

Create (no `id`) or save a draft, compare-and-set on `baseRevision`: `stateMismatch` "This draft changed in another window. Reopen it before editing." Refused while a send of it is live (`Draft.submissionId`). When `id` names an `incomplete` draft (written on another device, text not readable here) the reply's `draft.id` is a NEW local draft: use that id and its `revision` for later saves.
Discard a draft, cancelling any send of it that has not started; refused while it is sending. A draft with a live send (`Draft.submissionId`) also needs `send`, the scope that cancels a send.
Recipient type-ahead for To, Cc and Bcc: addresses you have written to or heard from, ranked by how much (the correspondents table), matching the start of a name or address.
Settle a draft changed on another device: keep mine, take theirs, or keep both (a copy). Refused while a send of it is live.
Sends in the outbox and their states.
Send with undo, send later, undo, send now, reschedule, send anyway after an unconfirmed send, retry a failed one, or cancel one that failed, is unconfirmed or missed its time.
Work that will not happen while Aplos is quit, for the ⌘Q warning: scheduled sends, reminders and unconfirmed sends.
The Later choices resolved by the engine's clock and zone: Today evening, Tomorrow, This weekend, Next week, Someday.
Upcoming reminders and fired ones not yet seen.
Mark fired reminders seen.

Queue AI work for a thread ahead of the background order (today's `ai.summarize`); the result arrives as a Summary change. Without `force`, a thread with a summary is left alone. `forbidden` (`ai.accountExcluded`) for an account left out of AI.
AI jobs, e.g. which threads are being summarized (today's `ai.summarizing`).

Suggest edits to a draft's text; the user's text stays until they choose. A `draftId` in an account left out of AI, or answering a thread there, is `forbidden` (`ai.accountExcluded`). Pasted text with no draft names the composing account in `accountId`, and one left out of AI is `forbidden` the same way; with neither, only the provider rule applies.

Write a draft or reply from an instruction, as a suggestion at the caret; a `threadId` or `draftId` in an account left out of AI (or a draft answering a thread there) is `forbidden` (`ai.accountExcluded`).
Speech to text for dictation, from audio uploaded with `Blob/put` (25 MB at most) on the Voice provider.
Cancel an interactive AI request, or all of them when `requestId` is absent.
The Follow up nudge for a thread, if the background job wrote one (absent with AI off or without consent).
Dismiss a Follow up nudge.
Settings → AI's provider table: status, where each key comes from, never the key.
A provider's models; local servers are asked live, hosted providers fall back to the curated list offline.
Whether each AI feature is ready, and why not.
Today's AI use against the daily background cap.
Save a provider key to the Keychain-backed vault; never echoed back.
Remove a saved key; refused for a key from the backend environment.
One cheap request with the provider's current key (usually its model list). No mail is sent. `message` is Aplos's own sentence for `reasonCode`, never the provider's text (FR-33).

One tiny request asking a model to call a tool, so a pass means Ask's tools work too. No mail is sent. A failure's message is Aplos's own sentence for its `reasonCode`, never the provider's text (FR-33).

Ask about your mail; returns at once with a run id, streams `progress` frames, and the answer lands in the Conversation. `scope.accountIds` and `context` only narrow the accounts whose "Use this account's mail for AI" is on; they never widen past them. A `context.draft.accountId` left out of AI is `forbidden` (`ai.accountExcluded`).
Stop a run, keeping the partial answer.

Accept or dismiss something Ask proposed (a reply, an event, a triage); accepting returns the receipt for Undo. Accepting an event with a guest other than you also needs `send`, and invites go out only then.
Three plain suggested questions.
Ask conversations.
Delete a conversation.
Start a setup session (onboarding, or "Show welcome" from Settings); background AI waits for its end.
End setup; idempotent, called by the renderer and by main on any window close, and always queues the one-shot backfill of unsummarised threads.
First sync's "Try again" for one account: resume from its checkpoint; idempotent while a run is going.
First-sync progress per account for the loading screen; also pushed as `Setup` state changes.
Add the demo accounts and their original demo mail; idempotent, never touches real accounts.
Put the demo accounts back to their starting mail; refused while sending.
Remove the demo accounts and their mail.
The stored consent for background AI and whether a provider or scope change needs it again.
Agree to background AI for the version shown, naming the provider and model on the card. Electron windows only: the owner must see the card (ARCH 8.3).
Withdraw consent; background AI stops.
The queue inspector: ops, AI jobs and submissions, content-free.
Retry a queued item now. Needs the scope of the method that made it (`QueueItem.scope`; `send` for a submission).
Discard a queued item. Needs the scope of the method that made it (`QueueItem.scope`; `send` for a submission).
The content-free diagnostics bundle, to preview before saving. Never uploaded.
The same bundle as a file blob, for main's save dialog (`File/save`).

Turn the verbose protocol log (headers only) on, switching itself off after 15 minutes, or off. A tool may only turn it off — turning it on is the owner’s. With no `on` it is a query and just answers the current deadline; the method stays a command and only the writes are audited.
Whether "Allow tools on this Mac" is on, and where.
Turn the local socket and loopback HTTP listener on or off (off by default in release builds).
Tools allowed on this Mac.
Allow a tool with scopes; the host writes its token to a 0600 file and the token never crosses the contract.
Revoke a tool; its open connections close within a second.
Sends, deletes and settings changes made by tools.
Accounts with health, capabilities, lease and identities; all of them when `ids` is absent.
Which provider an address or domain belongs to, with preset server settings (today's `account.discover` and `domain.check`). Round 1 connects Google only.
Start connecting an account; returns at once with a `connectId` and reports through `connect` frames (OAuth opens the browser via the host channel).
Sign in again (the weekly Gmail reconnect, `needsReauth`): passes `login_hint`, refuses another identity, keeps queued changes, no resync.

Reconnect an app-password or API-token account (iCloud, IMAP, Fastmail) with its new secret after `needsReauth`; reports through `reconnect` connect frames, keeps queued changes, no resync. `calendarSecret` replaces a separate CalDAV app password.

Full re-consent for missing scopes (installed apps cannot do incremental auth). `enable: calendarWrite` is the only way Aplos ever asks for permission to create, change and delete calendar events; without it the re-consent never asks for more than reading.
Cancel a connect still waiting for the browser; a late answer is then ignored.
Rename an account, change its colour, its notifications or "Use this account's mail for AI" (Electron windows only).
"Use this Mac" for background work (pin), or back to automatic; every account when `accountId` is absent (ARCH 6.5).

Remove an account and everything Aplos stored for it on this device; refused while one of its messages is on its way (sending, queued, scheduled, suspended or maybe sent) or a calendar change for guests is waiting. Failed sends are deleted with it.
Ask for a sync now; refused without any network call while an account is paused, unless `force` (once per throttle pause).
Whether Done, Later and reminders sync between your Macs on the encrypted channel.
Turn on device sync, joining with a pairing code from another Mac or creating one.
The pairing code to enter on another Mac.
Turn off device sync.
How this thread can be unsubscribed from: one-click (RFC 8058), mailto, a link to review, or not at all.
Unsubscribe (today's `thread.unsubscribe`): one-click POST or mailto where offered, else an https link to review.
Calendars with Aplos-side visibility and colour.
Show or hide a calendar in Aplos, or change its colour; never written to the provider.
Events and occurrences by id.
Create, edit or delete an event, for one occurrence, the series or the following ones; may notify guests, so it is held briefly for undo.
Hide events in Aplos only (the event detail's Hide), or show them again; never written to the provider, so nobody is told.
Answer an invitation for one occurrence or the series.
Find dates and meetings in a thread with the Plans model (today's `calendar.extract`); results are Plans to confirm. `forbidden` (`ai.accountExcluded`) for an account left out of AI.
Plans found in mail.
Add a plan to a calendar, with optional edits. Never with guests, so nobody is invited: add them afterwards with `Event/set`.
Dismiss a plan.
Block, lane and skip-Inbox rules.
Create (no `id`) or change a rule, e.g. "Always do this for [sender]" after a lane correction.
Delete a rule.
Block a sender: their mail goes to Spam now and later (today's `sender.block`).
Unblock a sender (today's `sender.unblock`).
Export your Aplos data (accounts, settings, workflow, drafts, conversations) as a file blob; no credentials.
